title: Compute brief - 20 November 2026
description: Washington priced the risk on both ends of the stack. The Senate voted to make data centres pay for their own grid, and a House committee published BIS licences for 879,868 H200 and MI325X chips approved for China, none shipped as of May. Wire: Senate BAAJA, China licence ledger, Shantou token-export cluster, Jordan Al-Risha sponsor, Brunei Rimba tender, Malaysia sovereign AI cloud. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: The grid bill goes to the tenant; the China ledger goes public.
lede: The Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act 62 to 33 on 19 November; it directs FERC to make data centres pay embedded and incremental transmission costs and sets ratepayer protections for loads of 20 MW or more. It now goes to the House. The same day the House Foreign Affairs Committee released BIS licence data: 3,444,160 Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X chips requested for Chinese buyers, 879,868 approved across 21 licences as of 11 May, every approval marked not shipped. California's attorney general subpoenaed Nvidia over China diversion and disclosure. Markets sold AI risk: the Nasdaq fell 2.25%, AMD 7.7% on a Hunterbrook short report, CoreWeave more than 6%, and Anthropic closed its first day at $97.17, up 17% on the $83 IPO price, before opening 9% lower on Friday. List prices held for a tenth day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.

watch.name: BAAJA in the House
watch.note: The House passed a narrower permitting bill last year; watch for conference or a straight vote before the Congress ends. FERC gets 270 days after enactment to revise transmission pricing.
